audit.whatIsWrong: win[] and phases[].side gave Cassiopeia six of seven stages including both item stages, contradicting whys[3], whys[5] and whys[6] and the 55.71% win rate.
audit.why: Cassiopeia has no dash and no blink. Once Gwen has her full kit plus Riftmaker, Hallowed Mist eats the poke and Skip 'n Slash closes a gap Cassiopeia cannot re-open. Her genuine windows are levels 2-3 before Gwen has W, and level 6 when Petrifying Gaze lands frontally.
audit.corrected: Skill / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Gwen / Cassiopeia / Gwen / Gwen.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page's core instruction is 'wait out Miasma's grounding' and 'bait the R', with no number attached to either.
audit.why: Miasma is 24/22/20/18/16 and Petrifying Gaze 120/100/80, against Skip 'n Slash at 13s and Hallowed Mist at 22s. A 24-second grounding means one whiffed Miasma buys you roughly two E windows — that is the concrete version of the advice the page was gesturing at.
audit.corrected: whys[2], spikes[2].text, wants.you[0] and mid now carry the real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twin Fang's healing is never mentioned, and the passive is described only as 'bootless move speed'.
audit.why: Twin Fang carries the heal flag and fires on a 0.75s cooldown against poisoned targets, so in the extended duel the page tells you to force she is healing off every tick she lands. Without Grievous Wounds the 'grind her squishy bar' plan is slower than the page implies.
audit.corrected: early, late and wants.you[1] now name Twin Fang's healing and the Grievous Wounds buy.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal item named anywhere despite an enemy who heals off her primary damage spell.
audit.why: Same flag as above; the item timing is the decision, and it belongs on the first-item spike rather than as an afterthought.
audit.corrected: spikes[3].text and wants.you[1] place Grievous Wounds at the Riftmaker/Nashor's spike.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are hers, not yours. Cassiopeia's Q (Noxious Blast) poison and Twin Fang chip you down before you have Hallowed Mist to hide in or Skip 'n Slash's on-hit range to touch her, and her W (Miasma) grounds your dash if you try to force it raw. Don't walk up to last-hit into her poison cloud — soak the minimum, eat the chip, and stay above half HP so her R never has a kill setup. You have no untargetability yet, so this is a farm-and-survive window; respect that Twin Fang deals bonus damage and refunds on a poisoned target, so every tick she lands speeds up her next one.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are hers, not yours. Cassiopeia's Q (Noxious Blast) poison and Twin Fang chip you down before you have Hallowed Mist to hide in or Skip 'n Slash's on-hit range to touch her, and her W (Miasma) grounds your dash for 24s at rank 1 if you force it raw. Do not walk up to last-hit into her poison cloud — soak the minimum, eat the chip, and stay above half HP so her R never has a kill setup. Twin Fang refires every 0.75s on a poisoned target and heals her as it goes, so every tick she lands both speeds up and repays her next one.

edits.before: Level 6 is the swing, and the order matters: HER 6 (Petrifying Gaze, the face-stun) beats you if you're caught facing her flat-footed, but YOUR 6 flips the lane. The play is to drop Hallowed Mist the instant her R or Miasma commits — the stun and grounding still land, but you keep snipping untargetably from inside the fog, and once the grounding window ends you E-dash on top of her and chain Needlework's slow so she can't kite. She's squishy with no dash or blink, so once you're in Snip Snip! range her poison can't out-trade Thousand Cuts plus your ability healing. Bait the R, mist it, dash in, and all-in.
edits.after: Level 6 is the swing, and the order matters: HER 6 (Petrifying Gaze, the face-stun) beats you if you are caught facing her flat-footed, but YOUR 6 flips the lane. Drop Hallowed Mist the instant her R or Miasma commits — the stun and grounding still land, but you keep snipping untargetably from inside the fog, and once the grounding ends you E-dash on top of her and chain Needlework's slow so she cannot kite. Her R is 120s at rank 1: bait it once and the next two minutes are yours. She has no dash or blink, so in Snip Snip! range her poison cannot out-trade A Thousand Cuts plus your healing.

edits.before: This is where you take over — but close it before she hits her own 2-item scaling. Your Riftmaker/Nashor's spike turns Snip Snip! into %-max-HP shred her squishy bar can't survive, and Hallowed Mist nullifies her only defensive layer since she has no escape. All-in on cooldown: wait out Miasma's grounding, E in, mist to eat the R, Q through her, and let Thousand Cuts plus ability healing eat her DPS. The danger is dragging it to her 2+ item window, where her bootless passive move speed and Miasma grounding let her kite you from outside mist and out-DPS your melee range. Win it at first item — don't gamble on the long game where the scaler pulls ahead.

notes: This matchup's prose is the best-researched in my slice - it already uses Noxious Blast correctly and already knows Miasma is the grounding. Two things were badly wrong around it. (1) content win[] gave Cassiopeia six of seven stages and the full phases matched, against a 55.71% Gwen win rate over 219 games and against its own whys[3], whys[5] and whys[6], which describe Gwen out-trading a no-mobility mage from her full kit onward. Corrected to Skill/Cassiopeia/Cassiopeia/Gwen/Cassiopeia/Gwen/Gwen. (2) The full layer refers to Cassiopeia as 'he' 26 times with no 'she' anywhere; corrected. Also added: Twin Fang heals her (kit heal flag) and no anti-heal was called anywhere, and no cooldown numbers existed on a page whose entire plan is 'wait out the grounding'. Miasma is 24s at rank 1 and Petrifying Gaze 120s - those are the two clocks this lane runs on.
